summary: Scheduled digest emails: tracehook query param sanitized to trace_hook, causing 404s and missing trace context
description: Issue summary: Customers receive scheduled digest emails for dashboard alerts, but the deep links back to the console lose trace context. The tracehook query parameter is being changed from 'tracehook' to 'trace_hook' by the email templating pipeline, and the console rejects the modified parameter, returning a 404 and therefore dropping trace linkage for all triggered alerts in the digest. Impact: - ClarityHealth reports missed trace links on scheduled alert digests for 18 dashboards across two orgs. - Customers cannot jump from an alert email to the associated console view, slowing investigation (support/CS escalation). - Loss of trace context causes SLO/alert correlation gaps for affected routes. Environment: - Prod (us-east) scheduled digest worker: alert-formatter v2.11.4, emailer v1.6.0, console v3.2.1 - Affected orgs: clarity-prod and clarity-staging (org merge history exists) Steps to reproduce: 1) Create a dashboard with an alert that includes a tracehook link (console -> scheduled alert config). 2) Add a high-cardinality route filter (route param in query string) to the scheduled alert. 3) Wait for scheduled digest run (or trigger via POST /api/v1/scheduled-runs). 4) Inspect email HTML body and the alert deep-link URL. Observed behavior: - Link in email HTML: https://console.redwood.dev/org/clarity-prod/dash/123?trace_hook=eyJ... (note underscore) - Clicking link returns console 404 and no tracehook context is attached to the session. Expected behavior: - Link should be: https://console.redwood.dev/org/clarity-prod/dash/123?tracehook=eyJ... and open console with trace context resolved. Preliminary investigation notes: - The email HTML is generated by alert-formatter service which calls the templating helper in emailer. The helper runs a sanitize pass to prevent XSS explosions in customer-supplied strings. - Trace: alert-formatter:v2.11.4 -> emailer:v1.6.0 -> sanitizer:mustache-sanitize@0.9.3 (internal fork). The sanitizer has a normalization rule that converts consecutive alphanumeric segments separated by non-alphanumeric chars into snake_case. In the sanitization step the parameter key 'tracehook' is seen in an interpolated fragment and the sanitizer rewrites it to 'trace_hook'. - Nginx edge and console validate the exact 'tracehook' parameter name; trace_hook is treated as unknown and rejected by the dashboard link handler (403 -> 404 surface). - The behavior was introduced after the sanitizer bump on 2026-02-28 during a templating dependency update. No change to console input validation was done concurrently. Next steps planned: - Short term mitigation: add an edge rewrite rule to map trace_hook -> tracehook for scheduled-digest endpoints in prod/us-east. (Workaround applied 2026-03-11 21:10 UTC for clarity-prod, verified links restored). - Medium term fix: remove the aggressive key-normalization from the sanitizer pipeline for alert URLs and add a whitelist exception for known tracehook keys. Create internal PR to revert or patch sanitizer behavior. - Long term: add automated unit test to alert-formatter/emailer that asserts no query-key rewrite for tracehook and add integration test covering scheduled digest email deep-linking. Related artifacts: - Sample broken email HTML (snippet): View dashboard - Sample expected URL: https://console.redwood.dev/org/clarity-prod/dash/123?tracehook=eyJhbGci...

2026-03-10 11:05 - Ethan Rivera (SRE): Reproduced in prod/us-east by triggering scheduled run. Confirmed parameter name rewrite in email body. Collected emailer and alert-formatter logs (attached to ticket).

2026-03-11 02:40 - Maya Chen (Platform Eng): Verified sanitizer upgrade on 2026-02-28. Locally reproduced sanitizer rule that normalizes 'tracehook' -> 'trace_hook' when parameter is generated via template interpolation.

2026-03-11 20:55 - Ethan Rivera (SRE): Rolled out temporary CDN rewrite mapping trace_hook -> tracehook for scheduled-digest domain on prod/us-east. Customer confirmed links now land on console and trace context restores.

investigation_notes: Sanitizer normalizes interpolated keys. Reproducible on local branch of sanitizer. No evidence of console-side change; console correctly enforces expected param name. CDN rewrite is a safe short-term mitigation but brittle for other keys. Need whitelist and tests.
workaround: Temporary CDN/edge rewrite mapping trace_hook -> tracehook applied in prod/us-east for scheduled-digest host. Customer notified. For customers in other regions, open support ticket to apply region-specific rule if impacted.
resolution: Mitigation applied (CDN rewrite) and verified on 2026-03-11. Code fix in progress: PR created to patch sanitizer (github.com/redwood/alert-service/pull/7342). INT-9012 tracks removal of aggressive key-normalization and test additions. Change will ship in alert-formatter v2.11.5.
notes_for_follow_up:
- Ensure migration plan in INT-9012 includes a canary and monitoring for scheduled-digest link failures.
- Add post-deploy synthetic that triggers a scheduled digest and validates returned email link contains 'tracehook' param exactly.
- Communicate to CS and customer once v2.11.5 is released with remediation steps.
